title: Operator Dynamics and Structural Constraints in L1 Obstruction Systems
description: This paper operationalizes the 'Evaluator Discipline' required for high-fidelity automated reasoning by formalizing the Operator Proposal Layer. In complex search and transport systems, proposal mechanisms often inadvertently contaminate the evaluation process by importing implicit heuristics or structure-as-truth. We strictly separate proposal generation (search) from gate evaluation (judgment under a declared policy). Operators propose candidate field evolutions omega -> omega' but carry zero acceptance authority: every accept/reject decision is a function only of the evaluator-computed obstruction tuple (Phi_1, Gamma_2, R_cl, Xi), the evaluator policy, and declared solver conventions—never of an operator's internal structure, parameters, or intent. We establish discrete coboundary defect foundations on finite connected directed graphs, cycle consistency equivalence, second-order closure defects Gamma_2 = ||d_1 h_1||_1 on 2-complexes, and local-green/global-red atlas gates. The framework enforces operator passivity, ensuring search systems can generate high-fidelity candidates while remaining structurally incapable of promoting their own authority. This monograph assigns no authorization and changes no jurisdiction.
